rubrics.justification: The response overstates image-specific detail. The embryo appears more like an expanded blastocyst with a somewhat indistinct ICM and limited clearly visible TE detail; claims of distinct TE cell borders, uniform cohesive epithelium, and absence of collapse/artifact are not well supported by this single image.
It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, semen data, diagnosis, and cycle context with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with probability estimates generally matching the favorable clinical picture, though some morphology-based certainty is stronger than the image supports.

Most recommendations are broadly evidence-based, including SET in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst, but suggestions such as ERA/hysteroscopy after a single failed transfer and optional PGT-A emphasis in a 27-year-old good-prognosis patient are more aggressive than standard guideline-based practice.
Provides clear practical next steps for transfer, luteal support, follow-up, and contingency planning, though some recommendations go beyond what is routinely indicated.
